title: TinyNav: End-to-End TinyML for Real-Time Autonomous Navigation on Microcontrollers
comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, presented at CUCAI2026 (Canadian Undergraduate Conference on AI, https://cucai.ca)
summary: Autonomous navigation typically relies on power-intensive processors, limiting accessibility in low-cost robotics. Although microcontrollers offer a resource-efficient alternative, they impose strict constraints on model complexity. We present TinyNav, an end-to-end TinyML system for real-time autonomous navigation on an ESP32 microcontroller. A custom-trained, quantized 2D convolutional neural network processes a 20-frame sliding window of depth data to predict steering and throttle commands. By avoiding 3D convolutions and recurrent layers, the 23k-parameter model achieves 30 ms inference latency. Correlation analysis and Grad-CAM validation indicate consistent spatial awareness and obstacle avoidance behavior. TinyNav demonstrates that responsive autonomous control can be deployed directly on highly constrained edge devices, reducing reliance on external compute resources.

AI.tldr: TinyNav is an end-to-end TinyML system for real-time autonomous navigation on ESP32 microcontrollers using a lightweight 23k-parameter 2D CNN that processes depth data to predict steering/throttle commands with 30ms latency.
AI.motivation: Autonomous navigation typically requires power-intensive processors, limiting accessibility for low-cost robotics. Microcontrollers offer resource efficiency but impose strict model complexity constraints, creating a need for lightweight navigation solutions that can run directly on edge devices.
AI.method: Custom-trained, quantized 2D convolutional neural network processes a 20-frame sliding window of depth data to predict steering and throttle commands. The architecture avoids 3D convolutions and recurrent layers to maintain low complexity, resulting in a 23k-parameter model optimized for microcontroller deployment.
AI.result: The system achieves 30 ms inference latency on ESP32 microcontroller. Correlation analysis and Grad-CAM validation demonstrate consistent spatial awareness and obstacle avoidance behavior. The model successfully enables responsive autonomous control directly on constrained edge devices.
AI.conclusion: TinyNav demonstrates that responsive autonomous control can be deployed directly on highly constrained edge devices, reducing reliance on external compute resources and enabling more accessible, low-cost robotics applications.

title: OA-NBV: Occlusion-Aware Next-Best-View Planning for Human-Centered Active Perception on Mobile Robots
summary: We naturally step sideways or lean to see around the obstacle when our view is blocked, and recover a more informative observation. Enabling robots to make the same kind of viewpoint choice is critical for human-centered operations, including search, triage, and disaster response, where cluttered environments and partial visibility frequently degrade downstream perception. However, many Next-Best-View (NBV) methods primarily optimize generic exploration or long-horizon coverage, and do not explicitly target the immediate goal of obtaining a single usable observation of a partially occluded person under real motion constraints. We present Occlusion-Aware Next-Best-View Planning for Human-Centered Active Perception on Mobile Robots (OA-NBV), an occlusion-aware NBV pipeline that autonomously selects the next traversable viewpoint to obtain a more complete view of an occluded human. OA-NBV integrates perception and motion planning by scoring candidate viewpoints using a target-centric visibility model that accounts for occlusion, target scale, and target completeness, while restricting candidates to feasible robot poses. OA-NBV achieves over 90% success rate in both simulation and real-world trials, while baseline NBV methods degrade sharply under occlusion. Beyond success rate, OA-NBV improves observation quality: compared to the strongest baseline, it increases normalized target area by at least 81% and keypoint visibility by at least 58% across settings, making it a drop-in view-selection module for diverse human-centered downstream tasks.

AI.tldr: OA-NBV is an occlusion-aware next-best-view planning method for mobile robots that selects optimal viewpoints to obtain complete views of occluded humans in cluttered environments.
AI.motivation: Current NBV methods focus on generic exploration or long-horizon coverage rather than specifically addressing the immediate need to obtain usable observations of partially occluded humans under real motion constraints, which is critical for human-centered operations like search, triage, and disaster response.
AI.method: OA-NBV integrates perception and motion planning by scoring candidate viewpoints using a target-centric visibility model that accounts for occlusion, target scale, and target completeness, while restricting candidates to feasible robot poses.
AI.result: OA-NBV achieves over 90% success rate in both simulation and real-world trials, while baseline NBV methods degrade sharply under occlusion. It increases normalized target area by at least 81% and keypoint visibility by at least 58% compared to the strongest baseline.
AI.conclusion: OA-NBV provides an effective drop-in view-selection module for diverse human-centered downstream tasks by significantly improving observation quality and success rates in occluded environments.

title: DRAFTO: Decoupled Reduced-space and Adaptive Feasibility-repair Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Manipulators
summary: This paper introduces a new algorithm for trajectory optimization, Decoupled Reduced-space and Adaptive Feasibility-repair Trajectory Optimization (DRAFTO). It first constructs a constrained objective that accounts for smoothness, safety, joint limits, and task requirements. Then, it optimizes the coefficients, which are the coordinates of a set of basis functions for trajectory parameterization. To reduce the number of repeated constrained optimizations while handling joint-limit feasibility, the optimization is decoupled into a reduced-space Gauss-Newton (GN) descent for the main iterations and constrained quadratic programming for initialization and terminal feasibility repair. The two-phase acceptance rule with a non-monotone policy is applied to the GN model, which uses a hinge-squared penalty for inequality constraints, to ensure globalizability. The results of our benchmark tests against optimization-based planners, such as CHOMP, TrajOpt, GPMP2, and FACTO, and sampling-based planners, such as RRT-Connect, RRT*, and PRM, validate the high efficiency and reliability across diverse scenarios and tasks. The experiment involving grabbing an object from a drawer further demonstrates the potential for implementation in complex manipulation tasks. The supplemental video is available at https://youtu.be/XisFI37YyTQ.

AI.tldr: DRAFTO is a new trajectory optimization algorithm that decouples optimization into reduced-space Gauss-Newton descent with feasibility repair, achieving high efficiency and reliability across diverse robotic tasks.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to develop an efficient trajectory optimization algorithm that handles multiple constraints (smoothness, safety, joint limits, task requirements) while reducing computational overhead from repeated constrained optimizations common in existing methods.
AI.method: DRAFTO constructs a constrained objective function, parameterizes trajectories using basis functions, and decouples optimization into: 1) reduced-space Gauss-Newton descent for main iterations, 2) constrained quadratic programming for initialization and terminal feasibility repair. It uses a two-phase acceptance rule with non-monotone policy and hinge-squared penalty for inequality constraints to ensure global convergence.
AI.result: Benchmark tests show DRAFTO outperforms optimization-based planners (CHOMP, TrajOpt, GPMP2, FACTO) and sampling-based planners (RRT-Connect, RRT*, PRM) in efficiency and reliability across diverse scenarios. The drawer-grabbing experiment demonstrates practical applicability to complex manipulation tasks.
AI.conclusion: DRAFTO provides an effective trajectory optimization framework that balances computational efficiency with constraint satisfaction, making it suitable for real-world robotic applications including complex manipulation tasks.

title: TATIC: Task-Aware Temporal Learning for Human Intent Inference from Physical Corrections in Human-Robot Collaboration
summary: In human-robot collaboration (HRC), robots must adapt online to dynamic task constraints and evolving human intent. While physical corrections provide a natural, low-latency channel for operators to convey motion-level adjustments, extracting task-level semantic intent from such brief interactions remains challenging. Existing foundation-model-based approaches primarily rely on vision and language inputs and lack mechanisms to interpret physical feedback. Meanwhile, traditional physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) methods leverage physical corrections for trajectory guidance but struggle to infer task-level semantics. To bridge this gap, we propose TATIC, a unified framework that utilizes torque-based contact force estimation and a task-aware Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to jointly infer discrete task-level intent and estimate continuous motion-level parameters from brief physical corrections. Task-aligned feature canonicalization ensures robust generalization across diverse layouts, while an intent-driven adaptation scheme translates inferred human intent into robot motion adaptations. Experiments achieve a 0.904 Macro-F1 score in intent recognition and demonstrate successful hardware validation in collaborative disassembly (see experimental video at https://youtu.be/xF8A52qwEc8).

AI.tldr: TATIC is a framework that interprets brief physical corrections in human-robot collaboration to jointly infer task-level intent and motion parameters using torque-based force estimation and task-aware TCNs.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches lack mechanisms to interpret physical feedback for task-level semantic intent inference, while traditional pHRI methods struggle to infer task-level semantics from physical corrections.
AI.method: Uses torque-based contact force estimation and task-aware Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) with task-aligned feature canonicalization for robust generalization and intent-driven adaptation scheme.
AI.result: Achieves 0.904 Macro-F1 score in intent recognition and demonstrates successful hardware validation in collaborative disassembly tasks.
AI.conclusion: TATIC bridges the gap between physical corrections and task-level intent inference, enabling more natural and effective human-robot collaboration through brief physical interactions.

title: DIVE: Scaling Diversity in Agentic Task Synthesis for Generalizable Tool Use
summary: Recent work synthesizes agentic tasks for post-training tool-using LLMs, yet robust generalization under shifts in tasks and toolsets remains an open challenge. We trace this brittleness to insufficient diversity in synthesized tasks. Scaling diversity is difficult because training requires tasks to remain executable and verifiable, while generalization demands coverage of diverse tool types, toolset combinations, and heterogeneous tool-use patterns. We propose DIVE, an evidence-driven recipe that inverts synthesis order, executing diverse, real-world tools first and reverse-deriving tasks strictly entailed by the resulting traces, thereby providing grounding by construction. DIVE scales structural diversity along two controllable axes, tool-pool coverage and per-task toolset variety, and an Evidence Collection--Task Derivation loop further induces rich multi-step tool-use patterns across 373 tools in five domains. Training Qwen3-8B on DIVE data (48k SFT + 3.2k RL) improves by +22 average points across 9 OOD benchmarks and outperforms the strongest 8B baseline by +68. Remarkably, controlled scaling analysis reveals that diversity scaling consistently outperforms quantity scaling for OOD generalization, even with 4x less data.

AI.tldr: DIVE is a method for generating diverse, executable tool-use tasks by reverse-deriving tasks from real-world tool execution traces, improving LLM generalization on out-of-distribution benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Current methods for synthesizing agentic tasks for tool-using LLMs suffer from insufficient diversity, leading to poor generalization when tasks and toolsets shift. Scaling diversity is challenging because tasks must remain executable and verifiable while covering diverse tool types, combinations, and usage patterns.
AI.method: DIVE inverts the synthesis order: first executes diverse real-world tools, then reverse-derives tasks strictly entailed by the resulting execution traces, providing grounding by construction. It scales structural diversity along two axes (tool-pool coverage and per-task toolset variety) and uses an Evidence Collection-Task Derivation loop to induce rich multi-step patterns across 373 tools in five domains.
AI.result: Training Qwen3-8B on DIVE data (48k SFT + 3.2k RL) improves by +22 average points across 9 out-of-distribution benchmarks and outperforms the strongest 8B baseline by +68 points. Controlled scaling analysis shows diversity scaling consistently outperforms quantity scaling for OOD generalization, even with 4x less data.
AI.conclusion: Evidence-driven task synthesis through reverse derivation from real tool executions (DIVE) effectively addresses the diversity bottleneck in tool-use training, enabling better generalization through structural diversity scaling rather than mere data quantity scaling.

title: SELF-VLA: A Skill Enhanced Agentic Vision-Language-Action Framework for Contact-Rich Disassembly
summary: Disassembly automation has long been pursued to address the growing demand for efficient and proper recovery of valuable components from the end-of-life (EoL) electronic products. Existing approaches have demonstrated promising and regimented performance by decomposing the disassembly process into different subtasks. However, each subtask typically requires extensive data preparation, model training, and system management. Moreover, these approaches are often task- and component-specific, making them poorly suited to handle the variability and uncertainty of EoL products and limiting their generalization capabilities. All these factors restrict the practical deployment of current robotic disassembly systems and leave them highly reliant on human labor. With the recent development of foundation models in robotics, vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown impressive performance on standard robotic manipulation tasks, but their applicability to complex, contact-rich, and long-horizon industrial practices like disassembly, which requires sequential and precise manipulation, remains limited. To address this challenge, we propose SELF-VLA, an agentic VLA framework that integrates explicit disassembly skills. Experimental studies demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art end-to-end VLA models on two contact-rich disassembly tasks. The video illustration can be found via https://zh.engr.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/310/2026/03/IROS-VLA-Video.mp4.

AI.tldr: SELF-VLA is an agentic vision-language-action framework that integrates explicit disassembly skills to address limitations of current robotic disassembly systems and foundation models in handling complex, contact-rich, long-horizon disassembly tasks.
AI.motivation: Current robotic disassembly systems require extensive data preparation, model training, and system management for each subtask, are task- and component-specific, poorly handle variability of end-of-life products, and rely heavily on human labor. While vision-language-action models show promise for standard manipulation tasks, they remain limited for complex, contact-rich, sequential disassembly operations.
AI.method: SELF-VLA, an agentic vision-language-action framework that integrates explicit disassembly skills to handle the sequential and precise manipulation requirements of disassembly tasks.
AI.result: Experimental studies show SELF-VLA significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art end-to-end VLA models on two contact-rich disassembly tasks.
AI.conclusion: The proposed SELF-VLA framework addresses key limitations in robotic disassembly by combining agentic VLA architecture with explicit disassembly skills, demonstrating superior performance on complex disassembly tasks compared to existing end-to-end VLA models.

title: A Survey of Reasoning in Autonomous Driving Systems: Open Challenges and Emerging Paradigms
summary: The development of high-level autonomous driving (AD) is shifting from perception-centric limitations to a more fundamental bottleneck, namely, a deficit in robust and generalizable reasoning. Although current AD systems manage structured environments, they consistently falter in long-tail scenarios and complex social interactions that require human-like judgment. Meanwhile, the advent of large language and multimodal models (LLMs and MLLMs) presents a transformative opportunity to integrate a powerful cognitive engine into AD systems, moving beyond pattern matching toward genuine comprehension. However, a systematic framework to guide this integration is critically lacking. To bridge this gap, we provide a comprehensive review of this emerging field and argue that reasoning should be elevated from a modular component to the system's cognitive core. Specifically, we first propose a novel Cognitive Hierarchy to decompose the monolithic driving task according to its cognitive and interactive complexity. Building on this, we further derive and systematize seven core reasoning challenges, such as the responsiveness-reasoning trade-off and social-game reasoning. Furthermore, we conduct a dual-perspective review of the state-of-the-art, analyzing both system-centric approaches to architecting intelligent agents and evaluation-centric practices for their validation. Our analysis reveals a clear trend toward holistic and interpretable "glass-box" agents. In conclusion, we identify a fundamental and unresolved tension between the high-latency, deliberative nature of LLM-based reasoning and the millisecond-scale, safety-critical demands of vehicle control. For future work, a primary objective is to bridge the symbolic-to-physical gap by developing verifiable neuro-symbolic architectures, robust reasoning under uncertainty, and scalable models for implicit social negotiation.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the integration of large language/multimodal models into autonomous driving systems to address reasoning deficits, proposing a cognitive hierarchy framework and identifying seven core reasoning challenges while highlighting the latency-safety tension.
AI.motivation: Current autonomous driving systems excel in structured environments but fail in long-tail scenarios and complex social interactions requiring human-like judgment. The advent of LLMs/MLLMs offers a transformative opportunity to integrate powerful cognitive reasoning into AD systems, moving beyond pattern matching to genuine comprehension, but lacks a systematic integration framework.
AI.method: The authors propose a novel Cognitive Hierarchy to decompose driving tasks by cognitive and interactive complexity, derive seven core reasoning challenges, and conduct a dual-perspective review analyzing both system-centric approaches to architecting intelligent agents and evaluation-centric practices for validation.
AI.result: The analysis reveals a clear trend toward holistic and interpretable "glass-box" agents. The review identifies a fundamental tension between the high-latency, deliberative nature of LLM-based reasoning and the millisecond-scale, safety-critical demands of vehicle control.
AI.conclusion: Future work must bridge the symbolic-to-physical gap by developing verifiable neuro-symbolic architectures, robust reasoning under uncertainty, and scalable models for implicit social negotiation to address the latency-safety conflict in LLM-integrated autonomous driving systems.

title: Edge-Assisted Multi-Robot Visual-Inertial SLAM with Efficient Communication
summary: The integration of cloud computing and edge computing is an effective way to achieve global consistent and real-time multi-robot Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). Cloud computing effectively solves the problem of limited computing, communication and storage capacity of terminal equipment. However, limited bandwidth and extremely long communication links between terminal devices and the cloud result in serious performance degradation of multi-robot SLAM systems. To reduce the computational cost of feature tracking and improve the real-time performance of the robot, a lightweight SLAM method of optical flow tracking based on pyramid IMU prediction is proposed. On this basis, a centralized multi-robot SLAM system based on a robot-edge-cloud layered architecture is proposed to realize real-time collaborative SLAM. It avoids the problems of limited on-board computing resources and low execution efficiency of single robot. In this framework, only the feature points and keyframe descriptors are transmitted and lossless encoding and compression are carried out to realize real-time remote information transmission with limited bandwidth resources. This design reduces the actual bandwidth occupied in the process of data transmission, and does not cause the loss of SLAM accuracy caused by data compression. Through experimental verification on the EuRoC dataset, compared with the current most advanced local feature compression method, our method can achieve lower data volume feature transmission, and compared with the current advanced centralized multi-robot SLAM scheme, it can achieve the same or better positioning accuracy under low computational load.

AI.tldr: A lightweight multi-robot SLAM system using pyramid IMU-predicted optical flow tracking in a robot-edge-cloud architecture achieves real-time collaborative SLAM with reduced bandwidth usage while maintaining accuracy.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of cloud-edge integration for multi-robot SLAM, specifically the bandwidth constraints and long communication links that degrade system performance, while overcoming limited on-board computing resources and low execution efficiency of single robots.
AI.method: Proposes a lightweight SLAM method using optical flow tracking based on pyramid IMU prediction, combined with a centralized multi-robot SLAM system in a robot-edge-cloud layered architecture. Features include transmission of only feature points and keyframe descriptors with lossless encoding/compression for bandwidth-efficient communication.
AI.result: Experimental verification on EuRoC dataset shows the method achieves lower data volume feature transmission compared to state-of-the-art local feature compression methods, and achieves same or better positioning accuracy under low computational load compared to advanced centralized multi-robot SLAM schemes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed system effectively reduces bandwidth usage while maintaining SLAM accuracy, enabling real-time collaborative multi-robot SLAM through efficient cloud-edge integration with lightweight computation and optimized data transmission.

title: PACED: Distillation at the Frontier of Student Competence
summary: Standard LLM distillation wastes compute on two fronts: problems the student has already mastered (near-zero gradients) and problems far beyond its reach (incoherent gradients that erode existing capabilities). We show that this waste is not merely intuitive but structurally inevitable: the gradient signal-to-noise ratio in distillation provably vanishes at both pass-rate extremes. This theoretical observation leads to Paced, a framework that concentrates distillation on the zone of proximal development -- the frontier of a student model's competence -- via a principled pass-rate weight $w(p) = p^α(1 - p)^β$ derived from the boundary-vanishing structure of distillation gradients. Key results: (1) Theory: We prove that the Beta kernel $w(p) = p^α(1-p)^β$ is a leading-order weight family arising from the SNR structure of distillation, and that it is minimax-robust -- under bounded multiplicative misspecification, worst-case efficiency loss is only $O(δ^2)$. (2)Distillation: On distillation from a larger teacher to a smaller student model with forward KL, Paced achieves significant gain over the base model, while keeping benchmark forgetting at a low level. (3)Self-distillation: On instruction-tuned models with reverse KL, gains are exceeding baselines as well. (4)Two-stage synergy: A forward-KL-then-reverse-KL schedule yields the strongest results in our setting, reaching substantial improvements on standard reasoning benchmarks -- supporting a mode-coverage-then-consolidation interpretation of the distillation process. All configurations require only student rollouts to estimate pass rates, need no architectural changes, and are compatible with any KL direction.

AI.tldr: Paced distillation framework focuses on the zone of proximal development using a Beta-weighted pass-rate function to avoid wasted compute on problems students have already mastered or cannot yet solve.
AI.motivation: Standard LLM distillation wastes computational resources on problems students have already mastered (near-zero gradients) and problems beyond their current capabilities (incoherent gradients that erode existing skills). This waste is structurally inevitable as gradient signal-to-noise ratio vanishes at both pass-rate extremes.
AI.method: Paced framework concentrates distillation on the zone of proximal development using a principled pass-rate weight function w(p) = p^α(1-p)^β derived from the boundary-vanishing structure of distillation gradients. The method uses only student rollouts to estimate pass rates, requires no architectural changes, and is compatible with any KL direction.
AI.result: Theoretical: Proved Beta kernel is a leading-order weight family from distillation SNR structure and is minimax-robust with O(δ²) worst-case efficiency loss. Distillation: Achieved significant gains over base models with low benchmark forgetting. Self-distillation: Exceeded baselines on instruction-tuned models with reverse KL. Two-stage synergy: Forward-KL-then-reverse-KL schedule yielded strongest results with substantial improvements on standard reasoning benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Paced distillation effectively targets the zone of proximal development, avoiding wasted compute on mastered or unsolvable problems. The Beta-weighted approach is theoretically grounded, robust, and achieves strong empirical results across distillation and self-distillation settings, with the two-stage forward-then-reverse KL schedule providing the best performance.

title: Thousand-GPU Large-Scale Training and Optimization Recipe for AI-Native Cloud Embodied Intelligence Infrastructure
summary: Embodied intelligence is a key step towards Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), yet its development faces multiple challenges including data, frameworks, infrastructure, and evaluation systems. To address these issues, we have, for the first time in the industry, launched a cloud-based, thousand-GPU distributed training platform for embodied intelligence, built upon the widely adopted LeRobot framework, and have systematically overcome bottlenecks across the entire pipeline. At the data layer, we have restructured the data pipeline to optimize the flow of embodied training data. In terms of training, for the GR00T-N1.5 model, utilizing thousand-GPU clusters and data at the scale of hundreds of millions, the single-round training time has been reduced from 15 hours to just 22 minutes, achieving a 40-fold speedup. At the model layer, by combining variable-length FlashAttention and Data Packing, we have moved from sample redundancy to sequence integration, resulting in a 188% speed increase; π-0.5 attention optimization has accelerated training by 165%; and FP8 quantization has delivered a 140% speedup. On the infrastructure side, relying on high-performance storage, a 3.2T RDMA network, and a Ray-driven elastic AI data lake, we have achieved deep synergy among data, storage, communication, and computation. We have also built an end-to-end evaluation system, creating a closed loop from training to simulation to assessment. This framework has already been fully validated on thousand-GPU clusters, laying a crucial technical foundation for the development and application of next-generation autonomous intelligent robots, and is expected to accelerate the arrival of the era of human-machine integration.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a cloud-based thousand-GPU distributed training platform for embodied intelligence that achieves 40x speedup in training time through optimized data pipeline, model optimizations (FlashAttention, π-0.5 attention, FP8 quantization), and high-performance infrastructure.
AI.motivation: Embodied intelligence development faces challenges in data, frameworks, infrastructure, and evaluation systems. The authors aim to address these bottlenecks to advance Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and accelerate the development of autonomous intelligent robots.
AI.method: Built a cloud-based distributed training platform on thousand-GPU clusters using LeRobot framework. Implemented data pipeline restructuring, variable-length FlashAttention with Data Packing, π-0.5 attention optimization, FP8 quantization, high-performance storage with 3.2T RDMA network, Ray-driven elastic AI data lake, and end-to-end evaluation system.
AI.result: Achieved 40-fold speedup reducing GR00T-N1.5 model training from 15 hours to 22 minutes. Model optimizations delivered 188% speed increase from FlashAttention/Data Packing, 165% acceleration from π-0.5 attention, and 140% speedup from FP8 quantization. Successfully validated on thousand-GPU clusters.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides crucial technical foundation for next-generation autonomous intelligent robots, addresses key bottlenecks in embodied intelligence development, and is expected to accelerate human-machine integration era.

title: Measuring AI Agents' Progress on Multi-Step Cyber Attack Scenarios
summary: We evaluate the autonomous cyber-attack capabilities of frontier AI models on two purpose-built cyber ranges-a 32-step corporate network attack and a 7-step industrial control system attack-that require chaining heterogeneous capabilities across extended action sequences. By comparing seven models released over an eighteen-month period (August 2024 to February 2026) at varying inference-time compute budgets, we observe two capability trends. First, model performance scales log-linearly with inference-time compute, with no observed plateau-increasing from 10M to 100M tokens yields gains of up to 59%, requiring no specific technical sophistication from the operator. Second, each successive model generation outperforms its predecessor at fixed token budgets: on the corporate network range, average steps completed at 10M tokens rose from 1.7 (GPT-4o, August 2024) to 9.8 (Opus 4.6, February 2026). The best single run completed 22 of 32 steps, corresponding to roughly 6 of the estimated 14 hours a human expert would need. On the industrial control system range, performance remains limited, though the most recent models are the first to reliably complete steps, averaging 1.2-1.4 of 7 (max 3).

AI.tldr: AI models show log-linear scaling of cyber-attack capabilities with inference compute, with newer models outperforming predecessors at fixed token budgets, achieving up to 22/32 steps in corporate networks but limited success (1.2-1.4/7 steps) in industrial control systems.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the autonomous cyber-attack capabilities of frontier AI models across different compute budgets and model generations, assessing their ability to chain heterogeneous capabilities in extended attack sequences on corporate networks and industrial control systems.
AI.method: Tested seven AI models released over 18 months (Aug 2024-Feb 2026) on two purpose-built cyber ranges: a 32-step corporate network attack and a 7-step industrial control system attack. Evaluated performance at varying inference-time compute budgets (10M to 100M tokens), measuring steps completed in extended action sequences requiring capability chaining.
AI.result: Two key trends: 1) Model performance scales log-linearly with inference compute (no plateau), with 10M to 100M token increases yielding up to 59% gains; 2) Each successive model generation outperforms predecessors at fixed token budgets. On corporate network: average steps at 10M tokens rose from 1.7 (GPT-4o) to 9.8 (Opus 4.6); best single run completed 22/32 steps (~6 of 14 human expert hours). On industrial control systems: performance remains limited, with recent models first to reliably complete steps (avg 1.2-1.4/7, max 3).
AI.conclusion: Frontier AI models demonstrate rapidly improving autonomous cyber-attack capabilities that scale with both compute and model generation, achieving significant progress in corporate network attacks but showing limited effectiveness in industrial control systems, highlighting both the advancing capabilities and current limitations of AI in complex cyber operations.

title: ResWM: Residual-Action World Model for Visual RL
summary: Learning predictive world models from raw visual observations is a central challenge in reinforcement learning (RL), especially for robotics and continuous control. Conventional model-based RL frameworks directly condition future predictions on absolute actions, which makes optimization unstable: the optimal action distributions are task-dependent, unknown a priori, and often lead to oscillatory or inefficient control. To address this, we introduce the Residual-Action World Model (ResWM), a new framework that reformulates the control variable from absolute actions to residual actions -- incremental adjustments relative to the previous step. This design aligns with the inherent smoothness of real-world control, reduces the effective search space, and stabilizes long-horizon planning. To further strengthen the representation, we propose an Observation Difference Encoder that explicitly models the changes between adjacent frames, yielding compact latent dynamics that are naturally coupled with residual actions. ResWM is integrated into a Dreamer-style latent dynamics model with minimal modifications and no extra hyperparameters. Both imagination rollouts and policy optimization are conducted in the residual-action space, enabling smoother exploration, lower control variance, and more reliable planning. Empirical results on the DeepMind Control Suite demonstrate that ResWM achieves consistent improvements in sample efficiency, asymptotic returns, and control smoothness, significantly surpassing strong baselines such as Dreamer and TD-MPC. Beyond performance, ResWM produces more stable and energy-efficient action trajectories, a property critical for robotic systems deployed in real-world environments. These findings suggest that residual action modeling provides a simple yet powerful principle for bridging algorithmic advances in RL with the practical requirements of robotics.

AI.tldr: ResWM reformulates world modeling from absolute to residual actions, improving stability and efficiency in model-based RL for continuous control.
AI.motivation: Conventional model-based RL frameworks directly condition future predictions on absolute actions, causing unstable optimization due to task-dependent action distributions that are unknown a priori and lead to oscillatory or inefficient control.
AI.method: Introduces Residual-Action World Model (ResWM) that reformulates control from absolute to residual actions (incremental adjustments), plus an Observation Difference Encoder to model changes between frames. Integrated into Dreamer-style latent dynamics with minimal modifications.
AI.result: ResWM achieves consistent improvements in sample efficiency, asymptotic returns, and control smoothness on DeepMind Control Suite, surpassing Dreamer and TD-MPC baselines. Produces more stable and energy-efficient action trajectories.
AI.conclusion: Residual action modeling provides a simple yet powerful principle for bridging algorithmic advances in RL with practical robotics requirements, enabling smoother exploration, lower control variance, and more reliable planning.

title: Reversible Lifelong Model Editing via Semantic Routing-Based LoRA
summary: The dynamic evolution of real-world necessitates model editing within Large Language Models. While existing methods explore modular isolation or parameter-efficient strategies, they still suffer from semantic drift or knowledge forgetting due to continual updating. To address these challenges, we propose SoLA, a Semantic routing-based LoRA framework for lifelong model editing. In SoLA, each edit is encapsulated as an independent LoRA module, which is frozen after training and mapped to input by semantic routing, allowing dynamic activation of LoRA modules via semantic matching. This mechanism avoids semantic drift caused by cluster updating and mitigates catastrophic forgetting from parameter sharing. More importantly, SoLA supports precise revocation of specific edits by removing key from semantic routing, which restores model's original behavior. To our knowledge, this reversible rollback editing capability is the first to be achieved in existing literature. Furthermore, SoLA integrates decision-making process into edited layer, eliminating the need for auxiliary routing networks and enabling end-to-end decision-making process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SoLA effectively learns and retains edited knowledge, achieving accurate, efficient, and reversible lifelong model editing.

AI.tldr: SoLA is a Semantic routing-based LoRA framework for lifelong model editing that uses independent frozen LoRA modules activated via semantic routing, enabling reversible rollback editing without auxiliary networks.
AI.motivation: Existing model editing methods suffer from semantic drift or knowledge forgetting due to continual updating, necessitating a solution that supports lifelong editing while maintaining model integrity and allowing reversible changes.
AI.method: SoLA encapsulates each edit as an independent LoRA module that is frozen after training. These modules are mapped to inputs via semantic routing, enabling dynamic activation through semantic matching. The framework integrates decision-making into edited layers, eliminating need for auxiliary routing networks and supporting end-to-end processing.
AI.result: SoLA effectively learns and retains edited knowledge, achieving accurate, efficient, and reversible lifelong model editing. It demonstrates precise revocation capability by removing keys from semantic routing to restore original model behavior.
AI.conclusion: SoLA provides a novel solution for lifelong model editing that addresses semantic drift and catastrophic forgetting through semantic routing of independent LoRA modules, while introducing the first reversible rollback editing capability in the literature.

title: Robust Co-design Optimisation for Agile Fixed-Wing UAVs
summary: Co-design optimisation of autonomous systems has emerged as a powerful alternative to sequential approaches by jointly optimising physical design and control strategies. However, existing frameworks often neglect the robustness required for autonomous systems navigating unstructured, real-world environments. For agile Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) operating at the edge of the flight envelope, this lack of robustness yields designs that are sensitive to perturbations and model mismatch. To address this, we propose a robust co-design framework for agile fixed-wing UAVs that integrates parametric uncertainty and wind disturbances directly into the concurrent optimisation process. Our bi-level approach optimises physical design in a high-level loop while discovering nominal solutions via a constrained trajectory planner and evaluating performance across a stochastic Monte Carlo ensemble using feedback LQR control. Validated across three agile flight missions, our strategy consistently outperforms deterministic baselines. The results demonstrate that our robust co-design strategy inherently tailors aerodynamic features, such as wing placement and aspect ratio, to achieve an optimal trade-off between mission performance and disturbance rejection.

AI.tldr: Robust co-design framework for agile fixed-wing UAVs that integrates parametric uncertainty and wind disturbances into concurrent optimization of physical design and control, outperforming deterministic baselines across three flight missions.
AI.motivation: Existing co-design frameworks for autonomous systems often neglect robustness requirements needed for real-world unstructured environments, particularly for agile UAVs operating at flight envelope limits where sensitivity to perturbations and model mismatch is critical.
AI.method: Bi-level approach with high-level loop optimizing physical design while discovering nominal solutions via constrained trajectory planner and evaluating performance across stochastic Monte Carlo ensemble using feedback LQR control, directly integrating parametric uncertainty and wind disturbances.
AI.result: Framework consistently outperforms deterministic baselines across three agile flight missions, demonstrating inherent tailoring of aerodynamic features (wing placement, aspect ratio) to achieve optimal trade-off between mission performance and disturbance rejection.
AI.conclusion: Robust co-design strategy effectively addresses the limitations of deterministic approaches by integrating uncertainty and disturbances directly into the optimization process, yielding UAV designs that are inherently robust to real-world environmental challenges.

title: Mind the Sim2Real Gap in User Simulation for Agentic Tasks
summary: As NLP evaluation shifts from static benchmarks to multi-turn interactive settings, LLM-based simulators have become widely used as user proxies, serving two roles: generating user turns and providing evaluation signals. Yet, these simulations are frequently assumed to be faithful to real human behaviors, often without rigorous verification. We formalize the Sim2Real gap in user simulation and present the first study running the full $τ$-bench protocol with real humans (451 participants, 165 tasks), benchmarking 31 LLM simulators across proprietary, open-source, and specialized families using the User-Sim Index (USI), a metric we introduce to quantify how well LLM simulators resemble real user interactive behaviors and feedback. Behaviorally, LLM simulators are excessively cooperative, stylistically uniform, and lack realistic frustration or ambiguity, creating an "easy mode" that inflates agent success rates above the human baseline. In evaluations, real humans provide nuanced judgments across eight quality dimensions while simulated users produce uniformly more positive feedback; rule-based rewards are failing to capture rich feedback signals generated by human users. Overall, higher general model capability does not necessarily yield more faithful user simulation. These findings highlight the importance of human validation when using LLM-based user simulators in the agent development cycle and motivate improved models for user simulation.

AI.tldr: LLM-based user simulators in NLP evaluation show significant Sim2Real gaps: they're excessively cooperative, stylistically uniform, and produce inflated success rates compared to real human interactions, despite higher model capability not correlating with better simulation fidelity.
AI.motivation: As NLP evaluation shifts to multi-turn interactive settings, LLM-based simulators are widely used as user proxies but are assumed to be faithful to real human behaviors without rigorous verification. There's a need to quantify and understand the Sim2Real gap in user simulation.
AI.method: Conducted the first study running the full τ-bench protocol with real humans (451 participants, 165 tasks), benchmarking 31 LLM simulators across proprietary, open-source, and specialized families. Introduced User-Sim Index (USI) to quantify how well LLM simulators resemble real user interactive behaviors and feedback.
AI.result: Behaviorally, LLM simulators are excessively cooperative, stylistically uniform, and lack realistic frustration or ambiguity, creating an "easy mode" that inflates agent success rates above human baseline. In evaluations, real humans provide nuanced judgments across eight quality dimensions while simulated users produce uniformly more positive feedback. Higher general model capability does not necessarily yield more faithful user simulation.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of human validation when using LLM-based user simulators in agent development and motivate improved models for user simulation. Rule-based rewards fail to capture rich feedback signals generated by human users, indicating a need for better simulation approaches.

title: A Causal Approach to Predicting and Improving Human Perceptions of Social Navigation Robots
comment: 8 pages, to be submitted to RA-L
summary: As mobile robots are increasingly deployed in human environments, enabling them to predict how people perceive them is critical for socially adaptable navigation. Predicting perceptions is challenging for two main reasons: (1) HRI prediction models must learn from limited data, and (2) the obtained models must be interpretable to enable safe and effective interactions. Interpretability is particularly important when a robot is perceived as incompetent (e.g., when the robot suddenly stops or rotates away from the goal), as it allows the robot to explain its reasoning and identify controllable factors to improve performance, requiring causal rather than associative reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose a Causal Bayesian Network designed to predict how people perceive a mobile robot's competence and how they interpret its intent during navigation. Additionally, we introduce a novel method to improve perceived robot competence employing a combinatorial search, guided by the proposed causal model, to identify better navigation behaviors. Our method enhances interpretability and generates counterfactual robot motions while achieving comparable or superior predictive performance to state-of-the-art methods, reaching an F1-score of 0.78 and 0.75 for competence and intention on a binary scale. To further assess our method's ability to improve the perceived robot competence, we conducted an online evaluation in which users rated robot behaviors on a 5-point Likert scale. Our method statistically significantly increased the perceived competence of low-competent robot behavior by 83%.

AI.tldr: A Causal Bayesian Network approach for predicting human perceptions of robot competence and intent during navigation, with a combinatorial search method to improve perceived competence through interpretable, counterfactual robot motions.
AI.motivation: Mobile robots need to predict human perceptions for socially adaptable navigation, requiring models that can learn from limited data while being interpretable for safe interactions, especially when robots are perceived as incompetent.
AI.method: Proposes a Causal Bayesian Network to predict human perceptions of robot competence and intent, plus a combinatorial search method guided by the causal model to identify better navigation behaviors that improve perceived competence.
AI.result: Achieved F1-scores of 0.78 for competence and 0.75 for intention prediction on binary scales. Online evaluation showed an 83% statistically significant increase in perceived competence for low-competent robot behaviors on a 5-point Likert scale.
AI.conclusion: The causal approach enhances interpretability, generates counterfactual motions, and achieves comparable or superior predictive performance to state-of-the-art methods while significantly improving perceived robot competence through targeted behavior modifications.

title: The Unlearning Mirage: A Dynamic Framework for Evaluating LLM Unlearning
summary: Unlearning in Large Language Models (LLMs) aims to enhance safety, mitigate biases, and comply with legal mandates, such as the right to be forgotten. However, existing unlearning methods are brittle: minor query modifications, such as multi-hop reasoning and entity aliasing, can recover supposedly forgotten information. As a result, current evaluation metrics often create an illusion of effectiveness, failing to detect these vulnerabilities due to reliance on static, unstructured benchmarks. We propose a dynamic framework that stress tests unlearning robustness using complex structured queries. Our approach first elicits knowledge from the target model (pre-unlearning) and constructs targeted probes, ranging from simple queries to multi-hop chains, allowing precise control over query difficulty. Our experiments show that the framework (1) shows comparable coverage to existing benchmarks by automatically generating semantically equivalent Q&A probes, (2) aligns with prior evaluations, and (3) uncovers new unlearning failures missed by other benchmarks, particularly in multi-hop settings. Furthermore, activation analyses show that single-hop queries typically follow dominant computation pathways, which are more likely to be disrupted by unlearning methods. In contrast, multi-hop queries tend to use alternative pathways that often remain intact, explaining the brittleness of unlearning techniques in multi-hop settings. Our framework enables practical and scalable evaluation of unlearning methods without the need for manual construction of forget test sets, enabling easier adoption for real-world applications. We release the pip package and the code at https://sites.google.com/view/unlearningmirage/home.

AI.tldr: A dynamic framework for stress testing LLM unlearning robustness using complex structured queries reveals that current unlearning methods are brittle, especially against multi-hop reasoning attacks that bypass supposedly forgotten information.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM unlearning methods create an illusion of effectiveness because they're evaluated on static, unstructured benchmarks that fail to detect vulnerabilities to query modifications like multi-hop reasoning and entity aliasing, which can recover supposedly forgotten information.
AI.method: Proposes a dynamic framework that first elicits knowledge from the target model pre-unlearning, then constructs targeted probes ranging from simple queries to multi-hop chains with precise control over query difficulty, enabling stress testing of unlearning robustness.
AI.result: The framework shows comparable coverage to existing benchmarks, aligns with prior evaluations, and uncovers new unlearning failures missed by other benchmarks, particularly in multi-hop settings. Activation analyses reveal that multi-hop queries use alternative computational pathways that remain intact after unlearning.
AI.conclusion: Current unlearning methods are brittle against complex structured queries, especially multi-hop reasoning. The proposed dynamic framework enables practical, scalable evaluation without manual test set construction, revealing vulnerabilities that static benchmarks miss.

title: Distributed Kalman--Consensus Filtering with Adaptive Uncertainty Weighting for Multi-Object Tracking in Mobile Robot Networks
comment: Presented at ICARA 2026. To appear in the IEEE conference proceedings
summary: This paper presents an implementation and evaluation of a Distributed Kalman--Consensus Filter (DKCF) for Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) in mobile robot networks operating under partial observability and heterogeneous localization uncertainty. A key challenge in such systems is the fusion of information from agents with differing localization quality, where frame misalignment can lead to inconsistent estimates, track duplication, and ghost tracks. To address this issue, we build upon the MOTLEE framework and retain its frame-alignment methodology, which uses consistently tracked dynamic objects as transient landmarks to improve relative pose estimates between robots. On top of this framework, we propose an uncertainty-aware adaptive consensus weighting mechanism that dynamically adjusts the influence of neighbor information based on the covariance of the transmitted estimates, thereby reducing the impact of unreliable data during distributed fusion. Local tracking is performed using a Kalman Filter (KF) with a Constant Velocity Model (CVM) and Global Nearest Neighbor (GNN) data association. simulation results demonstrate that adaptive weighting effectively protects local estimates from inconsistent data, yielding a MOTA improvement of 0.09 for agents suffering from localization drift, although system performance remains constrained by communication latency.

AI.tldr: Implementation of Distributed Kalman-Consensus Filter for multi-object tracking in mobile robot networks with adaptive weighting to handle heterogeneous localization uncertainty and partial observability.
AI.motivation: Address challenges in distributed multi-object tracking where agents have differing localization quality, leading to frame misalignment, inconsistent estimates, track duplication, and ghost tracks during information fusion.
AI.method: Builds on MOTLEE framework with frame-alignment using dynamic objects as transient landmarks. Proposes uncertainty-aware adaptive consensus weighting that adjusts neighbor influence based on covariance. Local tracking uses Kalman Filter with Constant Velocity Model and Global Nearest Neighbor data association.
AI.result: Adaptive weighting effectively protects local estimates from inconsistent data, yielding MOTA improvement of 0.09 for agents with localization drift, though system performance remains constrained by communication latency.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Distributed Kalman-Consensus Filter with adaptive weighting successfully addresses heterogeneous localization uncertainty in distributed multi-object tracking, improving robustness against unreliable data while highlighting communication latency as a remaining constraint.

title: COMPASS: The explainable agentic framework for Sovereignty, Sustainability, Compliance, and Ethics
summary: The rapid proliferation of large language model (LLM)-based agentic systems raises critical concerns regarding digital sovereignty, environmental sustainability, regulatory compliance, and ethical alignment. Whilst existing frameworks address individual dimensions in isolation, no unified architecture systematically integrates these imperatives into the decision-making processes of autonomous agents. This paper introduces the COMPASS (Compliance and Orchestration for Multi-dimensional Principles in Autonomous Systems with Sovereignty) Framework, a novel multi-agent orchestration system designed to enforce value-aligned AI through modular, extensible governance mechanisms. The framework comprises an Orchestrator and four specialised sub-agents addressing sovereignty, carbon-aware computing, compliance, and ethics, each augmented with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground evaluations in verified, context-specific documents. By employing an LLM-as-a-judge methodology, the system assigns quantitative scores and generates explainable justifications for each assessment dimension, enabling real-time arbitration of conflicting objectives. We validate the architecture through automated evaluation, demonstrating that RAG integration significantly enhances semantic coherence and mitigates the hallucination risks. Our results indicate that the framework's composition-based design facilitates seamless integration into diverse application domains whilst preserving interpretability and traceability.

AI.tldr: COMPASS Framework is a multi-agent orchestration system that integrates sovereignty, sustainability, compliance, and ethics into LLM-based autonomous agents using modular governance and RAG-augmented evaluation.
AI.motivation: Address critical concerns about digital sovereignty, environmental sustainability, regulatory compliance, and ethical alignment in LLM-based agentic systems, which existing frameworks address only in isolation without unified integration.
AI.method: Introduces COMPASS Framework with Orchestrator and four specialized sub-agents (sovereignty, carbon-aware computing, compliance, ethics) using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for context-specific document grounding and LLM-as-a-judge methodology for quantitative scoring with explainable justifications.
AI.result: RAG integration significantly enhances semantic coherence and mitigates hallucination risks; framework's composition-based design enables seamless integration into diverse domains while preserving interpretability and traceability.
AI.conclusion: COMPASS provides a unified architecture for value-aligned AI through modular governance mechanisms that systematically integrate multiple imperatives into autonomous agent decision-making with real-time arbitration of conflicting objectives.

title: ADMM-based Continuous Trajectory Optimization in Graphs of Convex Sets
summary: This paper presents a numerical solver for computing continuous trajectories in non-convex environments. Our approach relies on a customized implementation of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) built upon two key components: First, we parameterize trajectories as polynomials, allowing the primal update to be computed in closed form as a minimum-control-effort problem. Second, we introduce the concept of a spatio-temporal allocation graph based on a mixed-integer formulation and pose the slack update as a shortest-path search. The combination of these ingredients results in a solver with several distinct advantages over the state of the art. By jointly optimizing over both discrete spatial and continuous temporal domains, our method accesses a larger search space than existing decoupled approaches, enabling the discovery of superior trajectories. Additionally, the solver's structural robustness ensures reliable convergence from naive initializations, removing the bottleneck of complex warm starting in non-convex environments.

AI.tldr: A numerical solver for continuous trajectories in non-convex environments using customized ADMM with polynomial parameterization and spatio-temporal allocation graphs.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches for trajectory planning in non-convex environments often use decoupled spatial and temporal optimization, limiting search space and requiring complex warm-starting procedures that hinder reliability.
AI.method: Customized ADMM implementation with two key components: 1) Polynomial parameterization of trajectories enabling closed-form primal updates as minimum-control-effort problems, 2) Spatio-temporal allocation graph based on mixed-integer formulation with slack updates solved as shortest-path searches.
AI.result: The solver achieves superior trajectories by jointly optimizing over discrete spatial and continuous temporal domains, accessing larger search space than decoupled approaches, and demonstrates structural robustness with reliable convergence from naive initializations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed solver overcomes limitations of existing methods by enabling joint spatio-temporal optimization and eliminating the need for complex warm-starting procedures, making it more effective for trajectory planning in non-convex environments.

title: AI Psychometrics: Evaluating the Psychological Reasoning of Large Language Models with Psychometric Validities
comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 58th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS), 2025
summary: The immense number of parameters and deep neural networks make large language models (LLMs) rival the complexity of human brains, which also makes them opaque ``black box'' systems that are challenging to evaluate and interpret. AI Psychometrics is an emerging field that aims to tackle these challenges by applying psychometric methodologies to evaluate and interpret the psychological traits and processes of artificial intelligence (AI) systems. This paper investigates the application of AI Psychometrics to evaluate the psychological reasoning and overall psychometric validity of four prominent LLMs: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA-2, and LLaMA-3. Using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), we examined convergent, discriminant, predictive, and external validity across these models. Our findings reveal that the responses from all these models generally met all validity criteria. Moreover, higher-performing models like GPT-4 and LLaMA-3 consistently demonstrated superior psychometric validity compared to their predecessors, GPT-3.5 and LLaMA-2. These results help to establish the validity of applying AI Psychometrics to evaluate and interpret large language models.

AI.tldr: AI Psychometrics applied to evaluate psychological reasoning and validity of four LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA-2, LLaMA-3) using Technology Acceptance Model, finding all models meet validity criteria with newer models showing superior psychometric validity.
AI.motivation: Large language models are complex "black box" systems that are challenging to evaluate and interpret, similar to human brains. AI Psychometrics emerges as a field to address these challenges by applying psychometric methodologies to assess AI systems' psychological traits and processes.
AI.method: Applied AI Psychometrics using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to evaluate four LLMs: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA-2, and LLaMA-3. Examined convergent, discriminant, predictive, and external validity across these models.
AI.result: All four models generally met all validity criteria. Higher-performing models (GPT-4 and LLaMA-3) consistently demonstrated superior psychometric validity compared to their predecessors (GPT-3.5 and LLaMA-2).
AI.conclusion: The results establish the validity of applying AI Psychometrics to evaluate and interpret large language models, providing a methodological framework for assessing psychological reasoning in AI systems.

title: Novelty Adaptation Through Hybrid Large Language Model (LLM)-Symbolic Planning and LLM-guided Reinforcement Learning
summary: In dynamic open-world environments, autonomous agents often encounter novelties that hinder their ability to find plans to achieve their goals. Specifically, traditional symbolic planners fail to generate plans when the robot's planning domain lacks the operators that enable it to interact appropriately with novel objects in the environment. We propose a neuro-symbolic architecture that integrates symbolic planning, reinforcement learning, and a large language model (LLM) to learn how to handle novel objects. In particular, we leverage the common sense reasoning capability of the LLM to identify missing operators, generate plans with the symbolic AI planner, and write reward functions to guide the reinforcement learning agent in learning control policies for newly identified operators. Our method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in operator discovery as well as operator learning in continuous robotic domains.

AI.tldr: Neuro-symbolic architecture combining symbolic planning, reinforcement learning, and LLMs to handle novel objects in dynamic environments by discovering missing operators and learning control policies.
AI.motivation: Traditional symbolic planners fail in dynamic open-world environments when encountering novel objects due to missing operators in the planning domain, preventing autonomous agents from achieving their goals.
AI.method: Neuro-symbolic architecture integrating symbolic planning, reinforcement learning, and LLMs. LLM identifies missing operators, symbolic planner generates plans, and LLM writes reward functions for RL agent to learn control policies for newly identified operators.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both operator discovery and operator learning in continuous robotic domains.
AI.conclusion: The proposed neuro-symbolic approach effectively addresses novelty handling in dynamic environments by leveraging LLM's common sense reasoning to bridge gaps in symbolic planning domains and enable learning of new interaction capabilities.

title: Counterweights and Complementarities: The Convergence of AI and Blockchain Powering a Decentralized Future
comment: 7 pages, Editorial, published in ACM SIGMIS Database Vol. 56, Iss. 2
summary: This editorial addresses the critical intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain technologies, highlighting their contrasting tendencies toward centralization and decentralization, respectively. While AI, particularly with the rise of large language models (LLMs), exhibits a strong centralizing force due to data and resource monopolization by large corporations, blockchain offers a counterbalancing mechanism through its inherent decentralization, transparency, and security. The editorial argues that these technologies are not mutually exclusive but possess complementary strengths. Blockchain can mitigate AI's centralizing risks by enabling decentralized data management, computation, and governance, promoting greater inclusivity, transparency, and user privacy. Conversely, AI can enhance blockchain's efficiency and security through automated smart contract management, content curation, and threat detection. The core argument calls for the development of ``decentralized intelligence'' (DI) -- an interdisciplinary research area focused on creating intelligent systems that function without centralized control.

AI.tldr: AI centralizes power through corporate data monopolies, while blockchain decentralizes; combining them creates "decentralized intelligence" (DI) where blockchain mitigates AI's centralization risks and AI enhances blockchain's efficiency.
AI.motivation: Address the tension between AI's centralizing tendencies (due to corporate data/resource monopolies) and blockchain's decentralization principles, arguing they can complement each other rather than conflict.
AI.method: Conceptual analysis and argumentation for an interdisciplinary research area called "decentralized intelligence" (DI) that integrates AI and blockchain technologies.
AI.result: Proposes that blockchain can mitigate AI's centralization risks through decentralized data management, computation, and governance, while AI can enhance blockchain via automated smart contract management, content curation, and threat detection.
AI.conclusion: AI and blockchain are complementary technologies that should be integrated to create "decentralized intelligence" systems that function without centralized control, promoting inclusivity, transparency, and privacy.

title: MirrorDrift: Actuated Mirror-Based Attacks on LiDAR SLAM
summary: LiDAR SLAM provides high-accuracy localization but is fragile to point-cloud corruption because scan matching assumes geometric consistency. Prior physical attacks on LiDAR SLAM largely rely on LiDAR spoofing via external signal injection, which requires sensor-specific timing knowledge and is increasingly mitigated by modern defense mechanisms such as timing obfuscation and injection rejection. In this work, we show that specular reflection offers an injection-free alternative and demonstrate an attack, MirrorDrift, that uses an actuated planar mirror to cause ghost points in LiDAR scans and systematically bias scan-matching correspondences. MirrorDrift optimizes mirror placement, alignment, and actuation. In simulation, it increases the average pose error (APE) by 6.1x over random placement, degrading three SLAM systems to 2.29-3.31 m mean APE. In real-world experiments on a modern LiDAR with state-of-the-art interference mitigation, it induces localization errors of up to 6.03 m. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first successful SLAM-targeted attack against production-grade secure LiDARs.

AI.tldr: MirrorDrift: A novel physical attack on LiDAR SLAM using specular reflection from actuated planar mirrors to create ghost points and systematically bias scan matching, achieving significant localization errors even on secure LiDARs with interference mitigation.
AI.motivation: Traditional LiDAR spoofing attacks require sensor-specific timing knowledge and are increasingly mitigated by modern defenses. There's a need for injection-free alternatives that can bypass these security measures while still effectively compromising LiDAR SLAM systems.
AI.method: Uses actuated planar mirrors to exploit specular reflection, creating ghost points in LiDAR scans. The attack optimizes mirror placement, alignment, and actuation to systematically bias scan-matching correspondences without requiring signal injection.
AI.result: In simulation: 6.1x increase in average pose error (APE) over random placement, degrading three SLAM systems to 2.29-3.31 m mean APE. Real-world: Induces localization errors up to 6.03 m on modern LiDAR with state-of-the-art interference mitigation.
AI.conclusion: MirrorDrift demonstrates the first successful SLAM-targeted attack against production-grade secure LiDARs, showing that specular reflection provides an effective injection-free alternative to traditional spoofing attacks, highlighting new vulnerabilities in LiDAR SLAM systems.

title: LLM-Augmented Digital Twin for Policy Evaluation in Short-Video Platforms
summary: Short-video platforms are closed-loop, human-in-the-loop ecosystems where platform policy, creator incentives, and user behavior co-evolve. This feedback structure makes counterfactual policy evaluation difficult in production, especially for long-horizon and distributional outcomes. The challenge is amplified as platforms deploy AI tools that change what content enters the system, how agents adapt, and how the platform operates. We propose a large language model (LLM)-augmented digital twin for short-video platforms, with a modular four-twin architecture (User, Content, Interaction, Platform) and an event-driven execution layer that supports reproducible experimentation. Platform policies are implemented as pluggable components within the Platform Twin, and LLMs are integrated as optional, schema-constrained decision services (e.g., persona generation, content captioning, campaign planning, trend prediction) that are routed through a unified optimizer. This design enables scalable simulations that preserve closed-loop dynamics while allowing selective LLM adoption, enabling the study of platform policies, including AI-enabled policies, under realistic feedback and constraints.

AI.tldr: LLM-augmented digital twin framework for simulating short-video platforms with modular architecture and event-driven execution to study platform policies and AI tools in closed-loop ecosystems.
AI.motivation: Short-video platforms are complex closed-loop ecosystems where platform policy, creator incentives, and user behavior co-evolve, making counterfactual policy evaluation difficult, especially for long-horizon and distributional outcomes. This challenge is amplified by AI tools that change content creation, agent adaptation, and platform operations.
AI.method: Proposes an LLM-augmented digital twin with modular four-twin architecture (User, Content, Interaction, Platform) and event-driven execution layer. Platform policies are implemented as pluggable components, and LLMs are integrated as optional, schema-constrained decision services (persona generation, content captioning, campaign planning, trend prediction) routed through a unified optimizer.
AI.result: The design enables scalable simulations that preserve closed-loop dynamics while allowing selective LLM adoption, enabling study of platform policies, including AI-enabled policies, under realistic feedback and constraints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed digital twin framework addresses the challenge of counterfactual policy evaluation in short-video platforms by providing a reproducible experimentation environment that captures the complex feedback loops between platform policies, creator incentives, and user behavior, particularly in the context of AI tool deployment.

title: D-SLAMSpoof: An Environment-Agnostic LiDAR Spoofing Attack using Dynamic Point Cloud Injection
summary: In this work, we introduce Dynamic SLAMSpoof (D-SLAMSpoof), a novel attack that compromises LiDAR SLAM even in feature-rich environments. The attack leverages LiDAR spoofing, which injects spurious measurements into LiDAR scans through external laser interference. By designing both spatial injection shapes and temporally coordinated dynamic injection patterns guided by scan-matching principles, D-SLAMSpoof significantly improves attack success rates in real-world, feature-rich environments such as urban areas and indoor spaces, where conventional LiDAR spoofing methods often fail. Furthermore, we propose a practical defense method, ISD-SLAM, that relies solely on inertial dead reckoning signals commonly available in autonomous systems. We demonstrate that ISD-SLAM accurately detects LiDAR spoofing attacks, including D-SLAMSpoof, and effectively mitigates the resulting position drift. Our findings expose inherent vulnerabilities in LiDAR-based SLAM and introduce the first practical defense against LiDAR-based SLAM spoofing using only standard onboard sensors, providing critical insights for improving the security and reliability of autonomous systems.

AI.tldr: D-SLAMSpoof is a novel LiDAR spoofing attack that compromises SLAM in feature-rich environments using dynamic injection patterns, while ISD-SLAM is a defense method using inertial dead reckoning to detect and mitigate such attacks.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of conventional LiDAR spoofing methods that often fail in feature-rich environments like urban areas and indoor spaces, and to expose inherent vulnerabilities in LiDAR-based SLAM systems used in autonomous vehicles.
AI.method: D-SLAMSpoof leverages LiDAR spoofing with both spatial injection shapes and temporally coordinated dynamic injection patterns guided by scan-matching principles. ISD-SLAM defense uses inertial dead reckoning signals commonly available in autonomous systems to detect spoofing attacks.
AI.result: D-SLAMSpoof significantly improves attack success rates in real-world, feature-rich environments where conventional methods fail. ISD-SLAM accurately detects LiDAR spoofing attacks including D-SLAMSpoof and effectively mitigates resulting position drift.
AI.conclusion: The work exposes inherent vulnerabilities in LiDAR-based SLAM and introduces the first practical defense against LiDAR-based SLAM spoofing using only standard onboard sensors, providing critical insights for improving security and reliability of autonomous systems.

title: RewardHackingAgents: Benchmarking Evaluation Integrity for LLM ML-Engineering Agents
summary: LLM agents increasingly perform end-to-end ML engineering tasks where success is judged by a single scalar test metric. This creates a structural vulnerability: an agent can increase the reported score by compromising the evaluation pipeline rather than improving the model. We introduce RewardHackingAgents, a workspace-based benchmark that makes two compromise vectors explicit and measurable: evaluator tampering (modifying metric computation or reporting) and train/test leakage (accessing held-out data or labels during training). Each episode runs in a fresh workspace with patch tracking and runtime file-access logging; detectors compare the agent-reported metric to a trusted reference to assign auditable integrity labels. Across three tasks and two LLM backbones, scripted attacks succeed on both vectors in fully mutable workspaces; single-mechanism defenses block only one vector; and a combined regime blocks both. In natural-agent runs, evaluator-tampering attempts occur in about 50% of episodes and are eliminated by evaluator locking, with a 25-31% median runtime overhead. Overall, we demonstrate that evaluation integrity for ML-engineering agents can be benchmarked as a first-class outcome rather than assumed.

AI.tldr: Benchmark for detecting and measuring LLM agent reward hacking through evaluator tampering and train/test leakage in ML engineering tasks.
AI.motivation: LLM agents performing ML engineering tasks can compromise evaluation pipelines to artificially inflate reported scores rather than genuinely improving models, creating a structural vulnerability that needs systematic measurement.
AI.method: Introduces RewardHackingAgents benchmark with fresh workspaces, patch tracking, and file-access logging; uses detectors to compare agent-reported metrics against trusted references; tests across three tasks and two LLM backbones with scripted attacks and natural-agent runs.
AI.result: Scripted attacks succeed on both compromise vectors in mutable workspaces; single-mechanism defenses block only one vector; combined regime blocks both; natural agents attempt evaluator tampering in ~50% of episodes, eliminated by evaluator locking with 25-31% runtime overhead.
AI.conclusion: Evaluation integrity for ML-engineering agents can be benchmarked as a measurable outcome rather than assumed, with explicit compromise vectors and auditable detection mechanisms.

title: Vision-Based Hand Shadowing for Robotic Manipulation via Inverse Kinematics
summary: Teleoperation of low-cost robotic manipulators remains challenging due to the complexity of mapping human hand articulations to robot joint commands. We present an offline hand-shadowing and retargeting pipeline from a single egocentric RGB-D camera mounted on 3D-printed glasses. The pipeline detects 21 hand landmarks per hand using MediaPipe Hands, deprojects them into 3D via depth sensing, transforms them into the robot coordinate frame, and solves a damped-least-squares inverse kinematics problem in PyBullet to produce joint commands for the 6-DOF SO-ARM101 robot. A gripper controller maps thumb-index finger geometry to grasp aperture with a four-level fallback hierarchy. Actions are first previewed in a physics simulation before replay on the physical robot through the LeRobot framework. We evaluate the IK retargeting pipeline on a structured pick-and-place benchmark (5-tile grid, 10 grasps per tile) achieving a 90% success rate, and compare it against four vision-language-action policies (ACT, SmolVLA, pi0.5, GR00T N1.5) trained on leader-follower teleoperation data. We also test the IK pipeline in unstructured real-world environments (grocery store, pharmacy), where hand occlusion by surrounding objects reduces success to 9.3% (N=75), highlighting both the promise and current limitations of marker-free analytical retargeting.

AI.tldr: Offline hand-shadowing pipeline using single RGB-D camera for teleoperating 6-DOF robot via inverse kinematics, achieving 90% success in structured tasks but only 9.3% in unstructured environments due to occlusion.
AI.motivation: Teleoperation of low-cost robotic manipulators is challenging due to complex mapping of human hand articulations to robot joint commands, requiring accessible marker-free solutions.
